test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 13 Mar 2021 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: The work done by a force acting on an object is equal to the amount of force multiplied by the distance travelled in the direction of the force. Which of the following is NOT a unit of work?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kgm /sec2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Work is calculated as **Work (W)=Force (F)×Displacement (d)**.
 
• The SI unit of work is the Joule (J). Since force is measured in Newtons (N) and displacement in meters (m), we have** 1J=1N⋅m.**
 
• Also, from Newton’s second law, a Newton (N) can be expressed as **1N=1kg⋅m/s²**.
 
• **kg·m²/s²** is dimensionally equivalent to a Joule. This is a unit of work.
